subject: Discovery: Crestview Bank — private deployment & network/security constraints
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Thomas <emily.thomas@crestviewbank.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0500
Subject: Discovery recap — Crestview private deploy constraints and success criteria

Hi Emily / Rajesh — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed immediate next steps so we stay aligned. Notes below are based on what you shared; please correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points
- Current LLM vendors either require public endpoints or have limited on-prem support; you need no external egress for inference.
- Existing infra (OpenShift on-prem) has strict network segmentation and a dedicated security approval process.
- KMS/HSM requirement: keys must be customer-managed (BYOK) and never exported outside Crestview’s HSM vault.
- Auditability: detailed per-request logging + audit trail retention for 7 years.

Current stack / constraints you mentioned
- Compute: OpenShift 4.12 cluster with NVIDIA A40 GPUs in a secured rack.
- Networking: isolated VLANs, restrictive outbound ACLs (no internet except curated proxy), internal DNS only.
- Identity: SSO via Okta; RBAC must map to existing Crestview groups.
- Compliance: internal FedRAMP-like controls, plus quarterly penetration tests.

Success criteria for a short POC (what you want to validate)
1) Demonstrate inference inside the air-gapped environment with zero external egress.
2) Show KMS integration with Crestview HSM for model encryption keys and rotation policy.
3) Meet latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for <512-token requests on representative workload.
4) Auditability: per-request logs shipped to your SIEM (Splunk) and meeting retention requirements.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- We’ll share a short design doc and an offline installer for Private Control Plane and runtime (attachment: redwood_private_deploy_summary.pdf).
- Your team to share a sanitized network diagram and firewall rules (attachment: crestview_network_diagram.pdf).
- Schedule a 60-min deep-dive with your SecOps + Infra next week to walk the install flow and KMS integration (propose Wed 03/03, 10:00 AM ET).
- Vivek to draft the minimal config for OpenShift (node sizing, kernel params, GPU drivers).

Risks / open questions
- Will Crestview allow a customer-managed control plane appliance in a DMZ, or must the control plane be fully air-gapped with manual sync?
- HSM vendor and model — do you have a preference or certified list (e.g., Thales, AWS CloudHSM, on-prem Luna)?
- Any procurement gating items we should be aware of (PO thresholds, security questionnaires)?

Attachments included
- redwood_private_deploy_summary.pdf (high-level POC steps, offline installer notes)
- crestview_network_diagram.pdf (from your environment; please send updated sanitized version if available)

If this looks right I’ll get the installer/guide to you and lock the SecOps deep-dive. Appreciate the clarity — excited to move fast on a safe POC.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Emily Thomas <emily.thomas@crestviewbank.com>

Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 16:42:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Crestview private deploy constraints and success criteria

Thanks Sergio — this is a great summary and accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

Clarifications
- HSM: we use Thales Luna (v8) in our primary data center and have a DR instance in the secondary. BYOK must integrate with Luna via PKCS#11.
- Audit logs: Splunk ingest will be via a forwarder inside the cluster; logs must be JSON structured and include token-level usage metadata where possible.
- Control plane: goal is a closed control plane in our network with no outbound sync — any initial package must support offline updates via signed bundles.

Procurement & timeline
- Procurement window: approvals and PO in ~6 weeks once security signoff.
- POC target: internal stakeholders want a 4-week POC after signoff to validate latency and KMS flows.

Availability for deep-dive
- Wed 03/03 10:00 AM ET works for Rajesh and me. Please include a short agenda with the team roles so I can invite our SecOps lead and platform engineer.

Attachments we will provide before the call
- sanitized network diagram (we’ll remove IPs)
- brief SecOps questionnaire (15 items) — will send as PDF

Thanks — Emily
Emily Thomas
VP, Core Technology — Crestview Bank
emily.thomas@crestviewbank.com | (212) 555-2003
